answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying standing to attested useful work that decays over time. Each identity starts at zero and earns trust only as peers attest real service it performed, and the standing fades unless fresh work keeps renewing it. An attacker must therefore do genuine work for every fake identity, and the cost grows with each one, so flooding the network with empty shells buys nothing. A cedar grows slowly, and the delta between a fresh account and a seasoned one marks the zenith of real reputation.
